narrator: Mina Murray (letter), Lucy Westenra (letters), Dr. John Seward (phonograph diary), Quincey P. Morris (letter), Arthur Holmwood (telegram)
summary: Mina writes to Lucy from her work as assistant schoolmistress, practising shorthand and typewriting so she can help Jonathan, and teases Lucy about a rumoured tall curly-haired man. Lucy replies from 17 Chatham Street that it is Mr. Holmwood, and confesses she loves him; she also describes Dr. Seward, young head of a huge lunatic asylum. On 24 May Lucy receives three proposals in one day: Dr. Seward is refused gently, Quincey P. Morris of Texas is refused with great good humour and friendship, and Arthur Holmwood is accepted. On 25 May Seward, heartbroken, turns to work and begins a phonograph case-study of his patient R. M. Renfield, a strong, morbidly excitable man of 59. Quincey invites Arthur to a camp-fire dinner with Seward at the Korea the next night, and Arthur accepts by telegram. The chapter is a quiet, social interlude that introduces the future party of vampire hunters and the first hint of Renfield's danger.

scenes.title: Mina's letter of shorthand and ambition
scenes.summary: Mina apologises for the delay, describes her shorthand and typewriter practice, plans a journal, and mentions a short note from Jonathan in Transylvania saying he will return in about a week.
scenes.key_quote: I want to keep up with Jonathan's studies, and I have been practising shorthand very assiduously.

scenes.title: Lucy admits she loves Arthur
scenes.summary: Lucy explains the curly-haired man is Mr. Holmwood, describes the clever young asylum doctor who stares into faces, and confesses her love in a blushing rush.
scenes.key_quote: Oh, Mina, couldn't you guess? I love him.

scenes.title: Proposal one: Dr. Seward
scenes.summary: Seward, outwardly cool but nervous, nearly sits on his silk hat and plays with a lancet while proposing. Lucy refuses; he asks if she loves another, and leaves offering friendship.
scenes.key_quote: He kept playing with a lancet in a way that made me nearly scream.

scenes.title: Proposal two: Quincey Morris
scenes.summary: The Texan jokes in horse-harness slang, then earnestly asks if there is another. Lucy says yes; he asks for one kiss, receives it, and leaves as a friend without looking back.
scenes.key_quote: Little girl, I hold your hand, and you've kissed me, and if these things don't make us friends nothing ever will.

scenes.title: Proposal three: Arthur accepted
scenes.summary: Arthur comes in and in a moment has both arms around her; Lucy is overjoyed. Told only in a postscript.
scenes.key_quote: I am very, very happy, and I don't know what I have done to deserve it.

scenes.title: Seward's diary: study of Renfield
scenes.location: Seward's lunatic asylum (Purfleet, not named in this chapter)
scenes.summary: Seward, unable to eat or rest, throws himself into work, questions his quaint patient more closely than ever, and notes he was almost cruel in keeping him to his hallucination. He records a first clinical sketch of Renfield.
scenes.key_quote: R. M. Renfield, ætat 59.—Sanguine temperament; great physical strength; morbidly excitable.

scenes.title: Camp-fire invitation and telegram
scenes.summary: Quincey invites Arthur to a camp-fire dinner with Seward to drink to Arthur's happiness; Arthur wires acceptance with a hint of news.
scenes.key_quote: Count me in every time. I bear messages which will make both your ears tingle.

locations.name: 17, Chatham Street
locations.description: Lucy Westenra's London town house, where she and her mother receive callers; suitors find Lucy alone in the room.
features: a looking glass (Lucy studies her face in it)
a fireplace (Lucy recalls sitting by the fire undressing with Mina)

locations.name: Seward's lunatic asylum
locations.description: An immense private lunatic asylum under Dr. Seward's sole care, with wards of patients he visits.
locations.quote: he has an immense lunatic asylum all under his own care

locations.name: Quincey's camp-fire dinner (the Korea)
locations.description: Planned private dinner where Quincey and Seward will drink to Arthur; Seward and Quincey were pals 'at the Korea'.
locations.quote: There will only be one other, our old pal at the Korea, Jack Seward.

characters.name: Mina Murray

notable_lines: I want to keep up with Jonathan's studies, and I have been practising shorthand very assiduously.

characters.name: Lucy Westenra

characters.appearance: she studies her face in the glass; blushes and weeps easily
notable_lines: THREE proposals in one day! Isn't it awful!

characters.name: Dr. John Seward
characters.role: Twenty-nine year old head of a lunatic asylum, rejected suitor
characters.personality: resolute, calm, imperturbable on the surface, nervous within; clinical
characters.speech_style: straightforward, dignified; diary is analytical with Latin tags
notable_lines: Omnia Romæ venalia sunt. Hell has its price!

characters.name: Quincey P. Morris
characters.role: Wealthy Texan adventurer, rejected suitor, friend of Arthur and Seward
characters.appearance: young and fresh-looking despite many adventures
characters.personality: jolly, brave, chivalrous, well educated with exquisite manners
characters.speech_style: American slang with strangers excluded; horse and prairie metaphors
notable_lines: That's my brave girl. It's better worth being late for a chance of winning you than being in time for any other girl in the world.

characters.name: Arthur Holmwood
characters.role: Hon. Arthur Holmwood, accepted suitor, Lucy's fiance

characters.name: R. M. Renfield
characters.personality: sanguine temperament, morbidly excitable, periods of gloom ending in a fixed idea; possibly dangerous

puzzles.name: Reading Renfield's fixed idea
puzzles.setup: Seward questions Renfield to understand a hallucination whose centre he cannot identify.
puzzles.obstacle: Renfield's delusion is concealed behind gloom and excitability.
puzzles.book_solution: Seward pushes the patient to his point of madness and records observations; mystery unresolved.
puzzles.game_idea: Dialogue-deduction puzzle: choose questions to narrow Renfield's fixed idea while a cruelty meter rises and he closes up.
puzzles.quote: I questioned him more fully than I had ever done, with a view to making myself master of the facts of his hallucination.

dialogue_samples.speaker: Quincey P. Morris
dialogue_samples.line: Miss Lucy, I know I ain't good enough to regulate the fixin's of your little shoes, but I guess if you wait till you find a man that is you will go join them seven young women with the lamps when you quit.

dialogue_samples.speaker: Quincey P. Morris
dialogue_samples.line: I'm going to have a pretty lonely walk between this and Kingdom Come. Won't you give me one kiss?

dialogue_samples.speaker: Lucy Westenra
dialogue_samples.line: Yes, there is some one I love, though he has not told me yet that he even loves me.

dialogue_samples.speaker: Arthur Holmwood
dialogue_samples.line: Count me in every time. I bear messages which will make both your ears tingle.
